tasks.short: Read the request and prior test results, ask the patient about history and symptoms, and record the history in the exam record.

steps.what: Sonographer reads the request and prior test results
Sonographer obtains patient history from the patient
Sonographer records accurate patient history in free text

tasks.design: The imaging request in the radiology system ({OTHER}) shows earlier reports, images and relevant lab results for that body region in one view, so the sonographer does not search several screens. The sonographer records the history as today. Asking the patient stays with the sonographer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prior results were spread over several screens and history typed in free text.
tasks.enabler_now: Radiology systems can show prior results per body region and structured history fields.
tasks.still_hard: Patients do not remember earlier exams elsewhere.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing the symptom that changes where to look.

reach.learn: Whether history is complete at reporting.

evidence.claim: Radiology systems can show prior results per body region and hold structured history fields.
The dossier is kept 20 years and patients may ask who viewed it.

assumptions: Boundary: from the exam request to history recorded; scanning is outside.
Input contract: prior results in the hospital's systems; fallback is searching screens.
Asking the patient and recording the history keep their full time; structured fields instead of free text are not a saving. s1 keeps 60 because the one view replaces searching several screens.
research_questions: Do radiologists ask fewer follow-up questions?

incremental.description: No new work: the view is built from existing systems kept by the application team.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many priors sit in other hospitals' systems and are still searched (s1 keeps 80) (5.0); high: follow-up exams with priors in the view (10.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assist physicians during invasive procedures, coordinate timing with physicians and teams, and prepare equipment and materials.

steps.what: Ward staff and physicians update patient readiness and expected times on the room status board
Sonographer provides assistance during invasive procedures
Sonographer coordinates work with physicians and other team members by phone
Sonographer prepares equipment and materials for the procedure

tasks.design: A room status board in the radiology system ({OTHER}) shows which patient is ready, which room is free and when the physician is expected, so the sonographer phones less to coordinate. Assisting during procedures and preparing the room stay with the sonographer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Timing was agreed by phone between rooms and wards.
tasks.enabler_now: Radiology systems show room and patient status on boards.
tasks.human_edge: Holding the probe steady while the physician places a needle.

evidence.claim: Radiology systems can show room and patient status on boards.

assumptions: Boundary: from the procedure planned to the procedure assisted; the report is outside.
Input contract: wards and physicians update status; fallback is phone.
Ward staff and physicians update the board (s0) in about the time a phone call took; their time is outside the sonographer's savings. s2 keeps 70 because calls drop only where the board is current.

incremental.description: Sonographer updates room status on the board.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: wards rarely update the board, so most calls stay (s2 keeps 90) (1.4); high: a busy list with a current board (5.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Explain the procedure to the patient, transfer and position the patient on the ultrasound table, and scrub the skin and apply gel.

steps.what: Sonographer prepares the patient for the exam by explaining the procedure
Sonographer transfers the patient to the ultrasound table and positions the patient properly
Sonographer scrubs skin and applies gel

tasks.design: Patients get a short explanation video for their exam type in the patient portal with the appointment confirmation, so they arrive knowing what will happen and the explanation at the table is shorter. Transferring, positioning and preparing the skin stay with the sonographer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every patient heard the full explanation at the table.
tasks.enabler_now: Patient portals send exam information with appointments.
tasks.still_hard: Anxious patients need the explanation again anyway.
tasks.human_edge: Moving a patient in pain onto the table without hurting them.

reach.learn: Whether patients arrive better prepared, for example with a full bladder.

evidence.claim: Patient portals can send exam information and videos with appointment confirmations.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patient arrived to the patient ready; the scan is outside.
Input contract: videos made by the department; fallback is explaining at the table.
Patients watch a short video at home; priced as patient time.
Positioning and skin preparation do not change.
No focal upkeep: the department makes and keeps the videos.
research_questions: Do fewer exams fail for poor preparation?

incremental.description: Patients watch the explanation video before the exam.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few patients watch the video, so the explanation barely shortens (s1 keeps 95) (2.0); high: most patients watch it (6.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Enter exam data and measurements, write the preliminary findings sheet, send images and the sheet to the archive, collect pathology and post-operative reports, keep quality assurance records, and file correspondence.

steps.what: Sonographer enters exam data and measurements into the report
Sonographer interprets the sonographs and forms the preliminary findings
Sonographer writes the preliminary findings sheet with sonographs and interpretations
Sonographer checks the final findings sheet and images: patient, exam, measurements and findings, before they go to the radiologist
Sonographer sends the checked images and findings sheet to the archive for the radiologist
Sonographer collects pathology, biopsy and post-operative reports for quality assurance
Sonographer maintains quality assurance records in a spreadsheet

tasks.design: Measurements taken on the ultrasound machine are sent as structured data into the report in the radiology system ({OTHER}), so they are not typed again. The preliminary findings sheet is a structured template per exam type; the sonographer writes the findings, checks the sheet and images and sends them once to the image archive together. Pathology, biopsy and post-operative results are linked to the exam by patient and date, and a quality dashboard ({BI}) shows agreement between ultrasound findings and outcomes instead of a spreadsheet. Interpreting images stays with the sonographer and radiologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Measurements were retyped, outcome reports requested by e-mail and quality records kept in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Ultrasound machines send structured measurements; radiology systems link outcome reports to exams.
tasks.still_hard: Outcomes from other hospitals do not link automatically.
tasks.human_edge: Learning from a missed finding without blame.
tasks.altitude: The sonographer checks data and reads the dashboard instead of copying.

evidence.claim: Ultrasound machines can send structured measurements to radiology reports.
The dossier is kept 20 years and patients may ask who viewed it.

assumptions: Boundary: from the exam done to files kept; the radiologist's final report is outside.
Input contract: machines and pathology linked to the radiology system; fallback is retyping and e-mail.

Interpreting images, the sheet check and filing keep their full time. s1 keeps 30 for values the machine cannot send; s3 keeps 75 because the template gives the layout and the sonographer writes the findings; s4 keeps 20 for the send; s5 keeps 40 and s6 keeps 30 because outcomes link and the dashboard replaces the spreadsheet.
Quality figures are shown per department, not per sonographer, without works council consent.
unknowns: Exams with outcome reports per month.
research_questions: Is the correlation between ultrasound and pathology tracked for more exams?

incremental.description: Sonographer links outcomes from other hospitals by hand.

approvals.approved_version: The findings sheet and images for this patient and exam exactly as checked by the sonographer in s3c, sent once to the image archive for the reporting radiologist; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older machines send few measurements (s1 keeps 60) and many outcomes come from other hospitals (s5 keeps 70, s6 keeps 60) (30.7); high: linked machines and pathology (51.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The sonographer keeps asking, positioning, scanning and assisting; screen searching, retyped measurements and spreadsheet quality records shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A sonographer with more time scanning.
